observations.title: Test timing patterns: rolling window drift and subprocess timeout cascades
observations.content:
Two test failure patterns discovered in CI:

1. **Rolling window timestamp drift** — Tests with hardcoded dates (e.g., "2026-03-10") silently break when real time advances past the rolling window boundary (7-day or 4-hour windows). Fix: use `new Date(Date.now() - 60*60*1000).toISOString()` for timestamps that must stay within the window.

2. **Subprocess timeout cascade** — bun:test defaults to 5s per test. Quality-check tests spawning tsc/eslint/prettier can take 5-30s in CI. When first test times out, the sidecar's concurrency guard (`activeChecks.has(projectPath)`) still has the project locked, causing ALL subsequent tests to fail with "already running". Fix: add per-test timeouts via third argument to `it()`: `it("name", async () => {...}, 60_000)`.

Affected files: `src/sessions/usage-stats.test.ts`, `src/sidecar/quality-routes.test.ts`, `src/sidecar/client.test.ts`. Skill: `.claude/skills/sentinal-test-timing/SKILL.md`
observations.author: Evan Tiley

observations.title: Platform hook architecture: MCP (~5-20ms) vs Claude Code hooks (~50-200ms) vs OpenCode plugin (~1-5ms)
observations.content:
Decision framework for new sidecar-dependent features:

**Performance ranking:**
1. OpenCode plugin handler: ~1-5ms (in-process, single SidecarClient via closure)
2. MCP tool (both platforms): ~5-20ms (long-running process, single client at startup)
3. Claude Code hooks: ~50-200ms (NEW process per event, fresh connect each time)

**When to use each:**
- MCP tool: on-demand queries, user/AI-initiated operations
- Claude Code hook: must intercept/block tool calls (PreToolUse), or react to lifecycle events (SessionStart, PreCompact, UserPromptSubmit)
- OpenCode plugin: all event-reactive logic (tool.execute.before/after, event, session.compacting)

**Key gotchas:**
- OpenCode `tool.execute.after` `input.tool` uses built-in names ("write","edit","bash") — MCP tool calls have different names and won't match `MEMORY_TOOLS` filter
- Claude Code async hooks CAN return additionalContext but CANNOT return decision/block
- OpenCode `client.app.log()` writes to TUI only, NOT LLM context — use compact-state.json
- Claude Code subagent frontmatter supports `mcpServers` for scoping; OpenCode does not

Skill: `.claude/skills/sentinal-hook-architecture/SKILL.md`

observations.title: SHIPPED: worktree runtime isolation (issue #2) — 4 phases merged to main as c79e68c
observations.content:
Master plan docs/plans/2026-08-07-worktree-runtime-isolation.md — VERIFIED and squash-merged to main as c79e68c (137 files, +24069/-1627, 18 branch commits). Post-merge on main: 2476 pass / 0 fail, tsc clean, build:all + build:cli clean, all four runtime_* tools present in the compiled binary.

WHAT SHIPPED (4 phases): (1) shared-state guidance — DELETED the `lsof` port lines rather than adding a contradicting instruction; forbade copying the repo-root .env and terminating by name/pattern; tool-agnostic E2E; pkill/killall→ask opt-out on OpenCode only. (2) per-project slots, unique among LIVE worktrees (ready-to-merge IS live), slot 0 reserved for the main checkout, .env seeded from .env.example with the slot substituted. (3) .sentinal/runtime.json contract + runtime_config/runtime_init + /sync scaffolder. (4) runtime_up/runtime_stop — detached spawn into its own process group, worktree-local pidfile, ownership-verified teardown, stop-on-exit for abandon/squashMerge/cleanup.

SIX DIVERGENCES FROM THE ISSUE, each recorded as a decision: D4 no destructive-command guard (shell safety is user config; both platforms already provide the mechanism); D5 pidfile not a sidecar supervisor; D7 slot 0 reserved; D8 .env seeding; D10 three-state isolation map where absence = unknown and unknown NEVER prompts; D12 lifecycle borrowed from Playwright webServer + Testcontainers.

REVIEW CAUGHT REAL BUGS AT EVERY STAGE — the process earned its keep:
- Phase 2 plan review: my partial unique index was `WHERE status='active'`, but ready-to-merge is LIVE — would have freed the slot of a still-running worktree, reintroducing the exact collision.
- Phase 3 plan review: my strict interpolator rejected legitimate shell (`PORT=${PORT:-3000}`) AND didn't catch the bare-dollar `$UNSET` used to justify it. Narrowed to the ${SENTINAL_*} prefix.
- Phase 4 spec review (must_fix): realListGroup returned [] on ANY failure → {kind:"gone"} → stopOwnedGroup reported success and DELETED the ownership record while the orphan ran. Guard 5 authorised a directory deletion on a probe failure. Fixed with a third `unknown` state that fails closed. A test was pinning the wrong behaviour.
- Implementing agents refused two of my own bad instructions: Phase 3 Task 7 told them to write "shared is the effective default" (the pre-correction wording D10 exists to overturn) — refused and flagged. Phase 4 orphan-reap: I mandated verification then specified a row where verification is structurally impossible.

EMPIRICAL FINDINGS THAT ASSUMPTION WOULD HAVE MISSED:
- .git/info/exclude is DISPROVEN in both forms for linked worktrees — `git rev-parse --git-path info/exclude` resolves to the COMMON dir and leaks into the main checkout; the per-worktree copy is never read. Selected: tiered self-ignoring .gitignore.
- Claude Code reads ONLY `agent` and `subagentStatusLine` from a plugin-root settings.json — `permissions` there is INERT. That is why no CC permission default shipped; the ~45-entry allow-list was deleted.
- A bind-only port probe is WRONG on macOS: SO_REUSEADDR lets listen(P,"127.0.0.1") succeed while something holds 0.0.0.0:P. Now connects first.
- Ownership verification needs symlink resolution (/var→/private/var) or runtime_stop refuses to stop a process it just started.
- Bun.spawn({detached:true}) DOES call setsid() on POSIX so pgid===pid; stdio:["ignore",logFd,logFd] does NOT keep the parent alive (bun.d.ts:6503's warning applies to pipes, not real fds).
- OpenCode per-agent permission blocks MERGE with top-level (verified via GET /agent), so no duplication needed.

MY OWN ERRORS, RECORDED: marked Phase 4 VERIFIED while the enumeration-safety fix was UNCOMMITTED (a merge then would have silently discarded it); asserted client.ts "untouched at 582" for many turns when main was 573 — I was checking my expectation, not the baseline; `rm -f docs/plans/*.spec-review.json` deleted 28 unrelated review files (restored); dropped the master's Progress Tracking section in a restructure and a silent .replace() no-oped rather than erroring.

12 PIECES OF DEBT FIXED BEFORE MERGE, incl. pre-existing: squashMerge removed without --force and swallowed the error (slot released, directory survived — made far more reachable by R9 making runtime.json committable); stopOwnedRuntime failed OPEN; install.ts split 1057→222; `argument-hint: "..." or "..."` is invalid YAML so /spec shipped with NO frontmatter at all, in BOTH targets, because validate:plugin ends in `|| true`; LspClient test had NO timeout (the 30s belonged to the preceding test) while initialize() grants itself 10s and is called twice.

STILL OPEN: issue #3 (installer has no manifest — uninstall leaves 17 files on OpenCode); store.ts 836 / uninstall.ts 691 / spec-mcp-tools 681 / analysis-mcp-tools 602 all over the 600 block; validate:plugin still `|| true` and not in CI. RESIDUAL RISK (recorded in the plan): an UNCONFIGURED project can still reproduce incident steps 2-4 — the contract is opt-in and prose is the only barrier. registerWorktreeTools still degrades silently if worktreeConfig is omitted.

DON'T: run quality_report's prettier check project-wide on this repo — it reformatted 85 unrelated files (repo is not prettier-clean at HEAD under any 3.x; prettier isn't even a devDependency).
